articles.title: Swansea 0-1 West Ham: Divine Mukasa nets winner as Hammers sink Championship leaders
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Swansea City and West Ham United at the Swansea.com Stadium; Divine Mukasa scores the only goal as Nuno’s Hammers win at the home of the league leaders.
articles.body:
Divine Mukasa's calm first-half finish proved the difference on an afternoon when a new attendance record of 20,973 was set at the Swansea.com Stadium.

After West Ham's 6-0 thumping of Lincoln in midweek, this was a far more tactical affair but the importance of the win will not be lost on boss Nuno Espirito Santo.

The Hammers climb to second, above Middlesbrough on goal difference, and to within a point of Swansea, who lost at home for the first time since April.

Swansea had made their best start since 1923 by winning seven and drawing two of their opening 10 games.

The Welsh outfit also boasted the tightest defence in the Championship, while West Ham's 29 league goals at a rate of almost three per game was the highest in England's top four divisions.

There was a cup-tie feel to the occasion as the two teams battled for midfield supremacy, but openings were difficult to find.

The first shot of any description took 34 minutes to arrive - but the Hammers made it count.

Marko Stamenic was caught in possession and Pablo released Mohamadou Kante as Swansea defenders waited in vain for an offside flag.

Kante showed good composure on the by-line to pick out the unmarked Mukasa, who slotted home his third goal of the season.

It was only the third goal Swansea had conceded at home and the setback sparked the hosts in to action.

Adam Idah and Ronaldo had shots deflected wide in the space of a minute before Ben Cabango shook the underside of the crossbar.

Jay Fulton flighted a free-kick to the far post that was headed into Cabango's path by Moussa Yeo.

Cabango swivelled in a congested penalty area to strike the frame of the Hammers' goal, and Swansea were unable to force the ball home in the ensuing goalmouth scramble.

England international Jarrod Bowen had a quiet first half, but the Hammers skipper burst into life four minutes after the break to force a full-length stop from Lawrence Vigouroux.

It was the Hammers who were starting to look like league leaders as Vigouroux produced two excellent saves to deny Pablo and Bowen.

Idah fired just wide as Swansea rallied and Cabango made a hash of a bouncing ball in the penalty area as West Ham failed to clear Yeo's centre.

Substitute Stephen Eustaquio was off target and Idah headed over as Swansea began to ask serious questions of the Hammers' back line.

Bowen's mazy run deserved more than the careless finish from Manor Solomon that followed, but Ronald wasted a great chance to equalise in stoppage time.

"It was a really tight game and West Ham scored. They are an organised team who defends well, and it is hard to break them and push them back.

"We still did that and had some chances from set-pieces, and that's the story of the game.

"I would be much more concerned if we didn't create those chances and that's what we need to take from the game.

"Small things can make a difference, but what we can do now is try to improve.

"We just lacked a little bit of sharpness and conviction, but what I saw is we can compete against every team and just need to push ourselves on to beat the best teams in the league."

"We wanted not only to keep the momentum, but to build on it.

"I think it's been a good week that didn't start very well for us.

"It was a very demanding week in terms of the opponents we had to face, but it finished really well due to the hard work of the boys.

"The commitment, the unity and the way they played was really good against a very good Swansea side that had its chances also. It was a very intense football match."

articles.title: Bristol City 0-1 Sheffield United: Ollie Arblaster nets only goal in Blades win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bristol City and Sheffield United at Ashton Gate on Saturday; Ollie Arblaster scores the only goal early in the second half as Blades seal a narrow win.
articles.body:
The visitors took a fifth-minute lead when a headed clearance fell to Arblaster, who connected with a sweet right-footed volley from just outside the box which gave City goalkeeper Sam Tickle no chance.

It proved enough to settle a contest high on endeavour but low on entertainment from which the Blades emerged worthy winners.

For the Robins it meant a second home defeat in the space of four days without scoring a goal and their fans were quick to signal their frustration after nine minutes of stoppage time.

City midfielder Luke McNally made his first start in a home game since February 2025 when he sustained a serious knee ligament injury.

Yu Hirakawa and Rio Cardines also came in, while Blades manager Chris Wilder made five changes, bringing in Arblaster, Mark McGuinness, Harrison Burrows, Kalvin Phillips and Jordan Ayew.

The first half might have been a different story had Hirakawa capitalised on a golden opportunity to put City in front after four minutes. The winger broke clear, but with the goal gaping miscued his shot straight at United goalkeeper Michael Cooper.

The miss was made to look more costly when Arblaster fired United in front a minute later and they went on to look the better side in the opening period, winning most of the physical battles and easily nullifying City's predictable attacks.

Hirakawa did break away again in the 13th minute, this time going down under challenge inside the box but referee Ben Speedie waved away his penalty appeals.

Tom Cannon volleyed wide for United and Liam Kitching was unlucky to see a 27th-minute effort blocked for a corner as the Blades looked the more threatening outfit. The half-time whistle brought loud booing from City supporters.

Home boss Michael Skubala made two attacking changes at the start of the second half, sending on Elijah Adebayo and Jed Wallace for Scott Twine and George Tanner, but still his team failed to create much until two chances in quick succession in the 65th minute.

A Wallace shot was blocked by Burrows and from the resulting corner Dom Ballard headed over at the near post.

Soon United were pressing at the other end and Tickle did well to smother a Japhet Tanganga header on his line.

It was the visitors who looked more likely to score in the closing stages, Cannon having a shot blocked into the path of substitute Ryan One, who fired over from the rebound and also sent a late header wide.

City remained toothless and could have no complaints over the result.

"We weren't good enough today. We got bullied a bit.

"But we also had the best scoring opportunity of the game before they scored and had we taken it we would have seen a totally different game.

"When you are through on goal, you have to score. That's a problem for us at the moment. If you don't take your big chances and fail to keep clean sheets you are not going to win games.

"If you score early at home the opposition have to come out and play differently. But today they were too physical for us having gone in front.

"Today we started too slowly, lost too many duels and our clearances were not strong enough. We have a lot of work to do and it's good to have a free midweek coming up."

"That goal will do Ollie's confidence the world of good. When you suffer a serious knee injury and spend over a year out, the first thing you tick off is a return to training.

"Then comes a return to playing and after that a return to top form. It has been an up and down struggle for Oli to reach that stage.

"Today, he and Kalvin Phillips were brilliant in midfield. We all know how highly Oli was rated among young midfielders before the injury and what he is capable of achieving.

"We have had a lot chucked at us recently with the timing of the goals we have conceded and the quality of them, but today our game management was spot on.

"I was particularly pleased with our first-half performance. But we expected a reaction from Bristol City in the second half and dealt with a lot of balls into our box very strongly.

"The group is high on team spirit. I'm delighted to get a clean sheet and a solid away victory from a typical Championship game, which ebbed and flowed."

articles.title: Southampton 0-0 Bolton: Saint held at home by Trotters
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Southampton and Bolton Wanderers at St Mary's on Saturday; Saints frustrated at home by resilient Trotters as Tonda Eckert’s side are left frustrated.
articles.body:
The trio all wasted tap-ins, while Saints were also left bereft by a penalty not being given for a Ruben Rodrigues handball.

Bolton, on the back of away wins at Wolves and Norwich, could have claimed the three points themselves through Sam Dalby or Rodrigues.

But they made it 11 matches, spread over 25 years, without tasting defeat against Southampton, who have not lost at St Mary's for 18 games.

Bolton held a disciplined high line which frustrated the hosts' attacking attempts, with seven offsides called against Saints in the first half.

They only got into the Trotters' box three times despite dominating possession, but the first occasion saw Leo Scienza squander a golden chance.

James Bree produced a perfect cutback for Scienza, but the Brazilian could not keep his effort down.

The visitors' tight-knit defence refused to allow another such chance in the first half as Southampton were restricted to half-moments.

Scienza drilled a 30-yard shot straight at former Saints goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu while Larin could not quite get a touch on Scienza's in-swinging cross before the Canadian poked over via a deflection.

In fact, Wanderers forced the best save of the half two minutes before the break, when Thierry Gale's fierce drive was denied by Daniel Peretz's training hand.

The second half started off far more end-to-end; Xavier Simon's low shot bounced off Jack Stephens and narrowly wide.

And then at the other end, Lewis Dobbin - who replaced Larin before half-time, fired past the post when sent clean in behind by Scienza.

The hosts were denied a penalty by referee Matt Donohue when Scienza's cross from the left was blocked by the upraised hand of Rodrigues.

Bolton looked the more likely side to break the deadlock as they had three massive attacks.

Striker Sam Dalby's flicked header from a free-kick required a push over by Peretz and Rodrigues capitalised on some slack passing out from the back but saw his low effort deflected wide.

And Peretz pulled off a point-blank save to block out Josh Sheehan after the midfielder had bundled his way through the box.

Saints had their own golden chance in the 80th minute but Dobbin shinned a centre wide to set up a grandstand final 10 minutes, where both teams could sense three points but neither could take them.

Bree will have nightmares about his 84th-minute miss. He had the penalty box to himself, after Scienza's ball into the middle, but scuffed off-target to the whole ground's disbelief.

"There was a very clear situation on the cross and I think it is a clear penalty.

"The fourth official said that he thought he touched it with his head. I've got nothing to add.

"There is no point in talking about referees. In the end we are Southampton and we need to find a way to beat Bolton at home.

"I will look in the mirror at myself; there are probably a couple of decisions that I could have made better that could have won us the game.

"I have my opinion on some of the decisions but it doesn't help if I talk about that."

"It was a massive effort from us to get something from the game.

"We had to be really organised and disciplined to try and frustrate them as well as we could, but also be a threat when we had the ball.

"We created enough goalscoring opportunities to maybe nick one.

"Someone has told me that us and Millwall are the only teams not to concede a goal here, so that shows how much of an effort it has taken. It is also the first time they have dropped points at home.

"On another day we could have taken all the three points, but I'm not naive to know that we could have lost the game if a decision had gone for them - I think it should have been a penalty.

"We got away with one today and across this season we will need that bit of luck every now and again.

"We are playing well. We are standing up against opposition and competing - that is all you can ask for from a newly promoted team."

articles.title: Wrexham 4-1 Preston: Ben Whiteman scores as Red Dragons thump four
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Wrexham and Preston North End at the Racecourse Ground on Saturday; Ben Whiteman among the goals against his own club as Red Dragons pile more misery on struggling Lilywhites.
articles.body:
Joe Worrall scored his first goal in more than two years and, after Alfie Devine briefly brought Preston level, former Lilywhites midfielder Ben Whiteman struck next to score his first goal in Wrexham colours.

Sam Smith gave the hosts breathing space just before the hour and Kieffer Moore killed it off moments later.

In a week that had seen former Liverpool skipper Steven Gerrard linked with the manager's job, Wrexham's third league win of the season was a vital one as they moved up to 14th.

But Preston remain stuck on four points from 11 games, with Graham Alexander having lost his first three games in charge.

Parkinson got a big show of support from the home fans before kick-off but his side started on the back foot, with Worrall heading Odel Offiah's lobbed effort off the line before Andrew Hughes headed narrowly wide.

Parkinson had made four changes, bringing in Smith to add more firepower, but it took some time for them to start to put any pressure on struggling Preston.

Callum O'Hare's stabbed effort was pushed around the post by Daniel Iversen and Smith had a low shot saved before the breakthrough came from an unlikely source.

Worrall, a summer signing from Burnley, had not scored since a late winner for Besiktas against Rizespor in May 2024, but the big defender rose highest to head in Danny Imray's curled cross on his home debut.

That was a little bit of unwanted history for Preston, who equalled a club record set in 1969-70 for the longest run of league matches without a clean sheet at 26.

But Wrexham have been struggling at the back themselves this term, with their only clean sheet coming in a goalless draw with Swansea, and five minutes later the visitors were level.

Moore lost possession in midfield and Preston quickly worked it wide to Johnny Kenny. His angled shot was deflected but the ball fell for Devine who made no mistake for his first goal since March - and Preston's first since Alexander took over last month.

Wrexham's second was a painful one for the visitors. Imray's cross was only half-cleared and fell for former Preston man Whiteman to hit a low shot which left Iversen wrong-footed and the midfielder almost apologetically celebrating.

O'Hare might have killed it in first-half stoppage time as he burst into the box but his close-range shot was blocked.

Preston had chances to get back into it early in the second half but Brad Potts, just on as a substitute, missed the target at the end of a sweeping counter.

That quickly proved costly as Smith headed in Whiteman's corner moments later, with Moore then ending the contest as he flicked in Callum Doyle's low free-kick.

"I thought the lads stood up and were counted today individually and collectively.

"A lot of really solid performances from the lads.

"It was great to get back in with the lads on Thursday, galvanise the group, and look at the detail of where we needed to improve, and I thought the lads implemented (it) so well.

"I could go through a lot of individuals who I'm so pleased with, because we showed character, we showed mentality. It's an important win for us."

"We just conceded goals that we shouldn't. And I think if you look at the opportunities we had, certainly at the start of the second half when it was 2-1, if we take one of those it's potentially a different game.

"But we've got a little bit of a soft spot at the moment that gets exposed at this level and we have to work out how to fix it.

"I haven't got magic dust. We have to work. But I still think there's improvements and I have to look at whether I'm asking too much of the players at this moment considering where we are."

articles.title: Grimsby 0-2 Northampton
articles.summary: Northampton lifted themselves out of the relegation zone with their first away win of the season, beating out-of-form Grimsby 2-0 at Blundell Park.
articles.body:
Connor Lemonheigh-Evans had a header cleared off the line for the Cobblers after he met Lee Evans' free-kick to the back post, with Owen Dale having his follow-up shot diverted wide after a six-yard box scramble.

Matty Warhurst had two shots saved by Christy Pym in the first half before he then beat the Grimsby goalkeeper with a longer-distance strike in the 34th minute, firing with his right foot into the far bottom corner from the left channel.

Zach Jeacock then made strong stops from Iwan Morgan, Justin Amaluzor and Kieran Green to preserve Northampton's first-half lead.

Jamie Walker struck the upright and Charles Vernam blazed over from close range soon after the break for the hosts, before Jon Guthrie knocked in a second for Northampton after 58 minutes.

Edon Pruti was then sent off for Grimsby just three minutes later, leaving the field on a stretcher having suffered a nasty injury in the process.

articles.title: Iñigo Pérez: “Fallamos ocasiones demasiado claras”
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Villarreal lamentó las jugadas marradas durante la primera mitad
articles.summary: El técnico del Villarreal lamentó las jugadas marradas durante la primera mitad
articles.body: Iñigo Pérez considera que su equipo realizó una gran primera mitad, y que la ansiedad por fallara ocasiones “demasiado claras”, acabó pasando factura durante el partido. Iñigo aseguró que los cambios realizados de inicio no influyeron en el resultado final. Falta de pegada: “Las mismas preguntas y las mismas respuestas casi todos los partidos. Se viene manteniendo. La primera parte ha sido excelente. El Elche me parece un equipo dificilísimo, he visto todos sus partidos. Pero al descanso pudimos irnos con dos o tres goles de ventaja. Pero no se ha producido y ha aparecido la ansiedad por tener lo que crees que mereces. Pierdes el juego, fallas las circulaciones, con lo que atacas peor y le proporcionas ataques al rival. Ojalá en algún momento se rompa la estadística porque son ocasiones demasiado claras para llevarlas al entrenamiento y a la técnica” Ganar durante el proceso: “Los entrenadores se mantienen en los cargos por los resultados y no por los procesos. Podemos pensar que durante la ejecución de los procesos llegan los resultados, creo en ello pero sé que no es lo que a uno le sostiene. Entiendo cómo funciona la frustración, y yo lo estoy. Hay que seguir y ver que no hemos hecho bien en esa última media hora” ¿Demasiados cambios?: “No se sostiene que hayamos hecho nueve cambios y haya sido una de las mejores primeras partes, No tiene nada que ver que no hayamos ganado por los cambios. Y no se sostiene porque cuando han salido los teóricos titulares no hemos jugado tan bien. Logan y Carlos han estado muy bien. Pero el resultado hace que estas palabras no tengan eficacia” Bajón para el equipo: “A nivel emocional no estamos como el día del Nápoles, pero no creo que tenga una trascendencia para lo que viene. Si en Liverpool ganas o pierdes no es por lo de hoy. Hoy esperábamos ganas, el relato era precioso para ir a Anfield, pero este es el guion” Delanteros desacertados: “Han hecho goles toda su carrera y los volverá a hacer. No me generan dudas, son jugadores top y hay que ayudarlos y esperarlos” Maciá: "Estoy muy contento con el partido de Maciá. Ha estado muy bien en lo físico y táctico, y ha fallado un poco en lo técnico, donde es excelente. Pero no me preocupa. Los canteranos llevan un proceso diferente, llevan sus tiempos, no son como un fichaje. Estoy muy contento con su partido”. Jugar contra Iraola: “Me hace mucha ilusión verle, hablamos de manera continua. Mediáticamente no me gusta la exposición que voy a tener. Nos conocemos desde hace mucho, desde niños, jugamos juntos, fui su segundo. Será muy bonito e ilusionante, pero cuando pite el árbitro se acaba todo”

articles.title: Tremendo enfado de Luis García por el penalti y expulsión en contra del Mallorca: "Lo siento, pero esta no me la como"
articles.standfirst: "No se ha llevado a cabo el criterio que explican y con el que se llenan la boca", explicó el entrenador al final del encuentro
articles.summary: "No se ha llevado a cabo el criterio que explican y con el que se llenan la boca", explicó el entrenador al final del encuentro
articles.body: Al Mallorca se le escaparon dos puntos en Ipurua en un partido que comenzó ganando con gol de Adri Fuentes. Con 0-1, John Chetauya fue expulsado por un penalti sobre Iván Gil (vio la segunda amarilla en la jugada) cuando el futbolista armero ya había chutado un balón que se perdió por línea de fondo. Arnau Tenas detuvo el lanzamiento desde los once metros, pero los baleares disputaron el tramo final del encuentro en inferioridad numérica y los guipuzcoanos lo aprovecharon para terminar empatando con otra pena máxima en el tiempo añadido. Luis García, técnico bermellón, está muy molesto con las decisiones de Galech Apezteguia y lo explicó en la rueda de prensa postpartido. "Llevo muchos años en el fútbol. Confío y he confiado siempre en los árbitros. Los he defendido a capa y espada, pero la de hoy me cuesta mucho comérmela". "En ese primer penalti hay un contacto totalmente residual, algo que se han cansado de repetir los árbitros, el Comité, LaLiga y María Santísima. Son contactos residuales y nunca, nunca, y dicho por ellos, se iba a pitar penalti por eso. Y hoy, curiosamente, se pita un penalti que condiciona totalmente el partido. Lo siento, pero esta no me la como. No se ha llevado a cabo el criterio que ellos explican y con el que se llenan la boca". "Ese penalti no tiene ninguna explicación. Y ya no por el árbitro, sino por la gente que está en el VAR. El que me diga que eso es penalti, vamos... no sabe lo que es el fútbol ni un contacto residual".

articles.title: Swansea City 0-1 West Ham: Vitor Matos tells Swans to use defeat as fuel
articles.summary: Vitor Matos tells Swansea City to use the frustration of defeat to West Ham United as fuel in their bid to keep pace in the Championship promotion race.
articles.body:
Vitor Matos has told Swansea City to use the frustration of defeat by West Ham United as fuel in their bid to keep pace in the Championship promotion race.

Swansea's four-game winning streak came to an end as they lost in the league for only the second time this season thanks to Divine Mukasa's first-half goal.

The Swans, who remain top of the table despite defeat, had their chances against the second-tier title favourites, with Ben Cabango going closest when he hit the woodwork.

And Matos says the manner of the West Ham loss means it should not halt Swansea's early-season momentum.

"I think it's important that when the game finished we all felt that we could have taken something out of the game," said the Swansea head coach.

"I think that's the most important thing today, that we played against a really good opposition, a team that of course is one of the main contenders to go to the Premier League, and we felt that we can compete and we can beat them as well.

"That frustration, that's something that should stay, but that's something that more than anything should give us the fuel to push ourselves in training, push our standards and keep improving."

West Ham climbed to second in the table having become the first visiting side since Southampton in April to win a league game at Swansea.

The game was tight until Mukasa struck, but opened up from that point as Swansea went in search of an equaliser.

The hosts' two best chances fell to Cabango at set-pieces, with the centre-back rattling one shot against the bar and then dragging another wide of the target when he appeared to destined to equalise.

West Ham had further opportunities, with Lawrence Vigouroux making second-half saves from Jarrod Bowen – twice – and Pablo.

Matos felt Swansea proved their credentials despite losing a league game on their own ground for the first time since April.

"What I saw today, I think we can compete against every team and that's what we need to do," Matos added.

"We need to keep pushing ourselves to beat the best teams of the league. West Ham is one of the best teams.

"We tried [against them]. Unfortunately, we could not get something out of the game and that's the story."

articles.title: Man City 3-2 Ipswich: Boos and bananas on day of defiance at Etihad Stadium
articles.summary: Manchester City fans boo the Premier League anthem before watching their side move six points clear at the top of the table.
articles.body:
It started with Manchester City supporters booing the Premier League anthem and ended with Phil Foden taking an inflatable banana into his Match of the Day interview after helping see off Ipswich to pull six points clear at the top of the table.

On a day of defiance in east Manchester, City's fans made their feelings crystal clear in their first top-flight home game since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules .

Tens of thousands inside Etihad Stadium booed and jeered when the Premier League anthem was played over the speakers shortly before kick-off, then they started chanting 'City, City, City'.

There was a chant about playing Stockport away and the gallows humour continued when City fans sang 'You're going down with the City' to Ipswich 's travelling support.

City boss Enzo Maresca, who is the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge, said afterwards he felt the air of defiance from the stands even before kick-off.

"The environment was very good," said the Italian after a game watched by 60,817, a new record crowd at Etihad Stadium.

"The fans, the club and the players are all together on this journey."

City's best start since 1897 - but injuries a concern

City fans arrived at the ground to find hundreds of inflatable bananas had been placed on seats in the home sections for fans to wave throughout the game.

They were visible in the away end at Liverpool last week but this was on a different scale and the Etihad was turned into a sea of yellow.

The inflatables are a flashback to the late '80s when what began as a light-hearted joke soon turned into one of the most memorable fan crazes in English football.

They are enjoying a revival at a time when City have appealed after being found guilty of charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and creating 'sham contracts' to inflate sponsorship deals by £830m.

There were surreal scenes at one point on Saturday as fans jeered during the Premier League anthem while waving the inflatables in the air.

"You can tell they are behind us and they're pushing us," Phil Foden said when asked about the fans after scoring on his return to the side following suspension after being sent off against Manchester United on 13 September.

Foden's 19th-minute opener was his first goal of 2026.

"It's nice to play at home and you can hear how loud they are," he added. "They're giving us that extra boost that we need."

'I didn't expect to win seven out of seven'

Taking over from Pep Guardiola - 20 trophies during 10 seasons in charge - was always going to be a big challenge for Maresca.

Seven matches in, City's Premier League record remains flawless.

No points dropped, seven wins out of seven despite falling behind against Bournemouth and playing for more than an hour with 10 men at Manchester United .

"For sure I didn't expect to win seven out of seven," said Maresca. "We are working well and working good.

"I'm very happy especially with the situation in general.

"Today we controlled the game for 95 minutes. We created chances, we scored.

"We finished with a little bit of suffering together but overall, it is good."

On Foden's impressive return to action, Maresca added: "I said since day one that I love Phil. I know him from years ago and I know how good he is.

"It's a matter of helping him to again be one of the best players in the Premier League."

Despite the off-field turmoil, this is City's best start to a league season in 129 years.

Only Chelsea in 2005-06 (first nine) and Liverpool in 2019-20 (first eight) have ever won the first seven matches of a Premier League campaign.

"First of all, I am very happy because it's a matter of winning games in this business," said Maresca after the game.

"We were able to win seven in a row and what made me very happy was day by day with the players, the way they are working and how I can see them improving.

"Today I thought we controlled the game, created chances and [were] good off the ball. We are doing well and I think that's the most important thing."

On his players dealing with the events surrounding the club off the field, Maresca said: "They are not worried about people who judge from outside because they know people are trying to judge them.

"Inside, I promise the players are happy. They're getting credit and I give credit to them."

articles.title: Celtic Keeper Shaken Again As Per Charlie Mulgrew: Can O’Neill Trust Anyone Between The Sticks?
articles.summary: A 4-1 beating in Lisbon stings. What stung Celtic fans most, though, was how two of those goals arrived.Viljami Sinisalo had only just won the gloves back. S...
articles.body:
A 4-1 beating in Lisbon stings. What stung Celtic fans most, though, was how two of those goals arrived.

Viljami Sinisalo had only just won the gloves back. Sam Johnstone lost them after a ropey League Cup afternoon at Ibrox, so Martin O'Neill gave the Finn another go. Alexander Bah then made it 2-0 to Benfica, and Sinisalo couldn't keep it out. Jhon Duran later poked a close-range finish through his legs.

Two straight Europa League defeats leave Celtic with a stiff task to reach the knockouts.

Charlie Mulgrew didn't dress it up. Speaking to Premier Sports Ireland, as relayed by Celts Are Here , the former Celtic defender said Sinisalo is "still scratching for a number one". He added that the 25-year-old keeps failing to make the saves Europe demands.

Mulgrew also reckons O'Neill hasn't found his best XI, and the weak spots keep costing them at this level. Fans can't really argue. A keeper lives under a microscope, yet the criticism has bite, since every decent side starts at the back. Johnstone could return, though few expect him to change much while question marks hang over defence and midfield.

"Sinisalo, for me… still scratching for a number one.

"Johnstone's came in, had a bad time at Ibrox, then came out of the team; Sinisalo back in.

"But continually in Europe, for me, Sinisalo doesn't make the necessary saves."

Can O'Neill settle on a goalkeeper while the defence keeps leaking?

GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – JULY 25: Viljami Sinisalo of Celtic arrives at the ground ahead of kick off in the Celtic v AC Milan in a pre-season friendly at Celtic Park on July 25, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by WM Sport Media/Getty Images)

From O'Neill's chair, the gloves aren't the real itch. Sinisalo gave him two soft ones in one night, but dropping a 25-year-old again could flatten whatever confidence he has left, and Johnstone's Ibrox wobble leaves no obvious alternative. So O'Neill sticks, probably, and hopes.

A keeper can't save what a back four lets through. Benfica found space far too easily, and O'Neill knows a settled defence protects either goalkeeper better than any swap. He needs to pick his back four, pick his midfield screen, and leave them alone for a month. Constant tinkering is how you end up losing 4-1.

Johnstone deserves a go in a domestic game, where a mistake won't cost a European place. Sinisalo keeps the Thursday nights for now, because chopping and changing sends the loudest message of all: nobody's sure.

A quiet word and a clean sheet against a modest league side could do more for Sinisalo than any team talk. Mulgrew has a point about Europe, mind. Domestic games hide flaws. Europe shows them off.

articles.title: El Inter vuelve a ser el Dr. Jekyll en Bolonia
articles.standfirst: Los 'nerazzurri', negados en Champions, se sitúan líderes en solitario en la Serie A
articles.summary: Los 'nerazzurri', negados en Champions, se sitúan líderes en solitario en la Serie A
articles.body: Esta temporada nos está mostrando un Inter de dos caras. Los 'nerazzurri' son 'Mr. Hyde' en Champions, donde cuentan sus dos partidos por derrotas. En Serie A no hay quien les tosa. A la espera de lo que haga la Lazio, la victoria ante el Bolonia (1-3) les sitúa líderes en solitario con 19 puntos de 21 posibles. El partido, paradójicamente, no pudo empezar peor para los de Cristian Chivu. Juan Miranda interceptó un mal pase en salida, Pobega se marchó con potencia de Luiz Henrique y Bisseck y batió a Josep Martínez con un potente zurdazo. Se reivindicó el portero español con una buena parada a un misil de Bernardeschi en el 16'. Pudo marcar nuevamente Pobega en el 38', pero su disparo salió rozando el poste. Poco a poco, sin embargo, el Inter comenzó a inclinar el campo. Lo aprovechó Marcus Thuram para poner el 1-1 en el 44' con un extraordinario cabezazo a la escuadra a centro de Barella desde la derecha. Pudieron, incluso, irse ganando al descanso. Lo evitó Skorupski en el añadido al salvar un remate de Pio Esposito en boca de gol. El 1-2 era cuestión de tiempo. Llegó en el 69'. Dobló Luiz Henrique para Zielinski y éste sirvió el pase de la muerte para que Carlos Augusto marcara a placer. Los 'nerazzurri' seguían acumulando ocasiones de peligro. Petar Sucic falló un gol a puerta vacía en el 76': remató al poste. Poco después, en el 81', le anularon un golazo a Ange Bony. Bastoni filtró un pase en largo para el atacante y éste hizo el resto: se zafó de Darmian y superó a Skorupski mano a mano. Bony se 'vengó' anotando el definitivo 1-3 en el 83'. Mkhitaryan se inventó un control magistral y dobló sobre la subida por izquierda de Carlos Augusto, que sirvió el gol en bandeja a Bony. El Inter vuelve a ser el 'Dr. Jekyll'.

articles.body:
Saturday's game between Real Betis and Barcelona has given neutral fans quite some drama to soak up.

We've seen a host equalizer ruled out, as Hansi Flick and company held a 2-1 lead at the break. Then three more goals followed immediately after the restart, and a red card was issued.

Amidst all the chaos, the send-off will take centre stage.

Facundo Bernal was given marching orders after arguing with Fermín López, who was down on the ground and apparently injured.

During the exchange, Lamine Yamal flew in at the Real Betis man and shoved him. Bernal then grabbed the Barcelona wonderkid by the head and headbutted him before seeing direct red.

The scrappy affair also earned Yamal a yellow card of his own.

articles.title: Finally finding club form, USMNT star Gio Reyna flourishing with goal against PSG in Ligue 1
articles.summary: Gio Reyna has been a regular for the U.S. national team under Mauricio Pochettino since returning to the national team fold in late 2025, but it has not alwa...
articles.body:
Gio Reyna has been a regular for the U.S. national team under Mauricio Pochettino since returning to the national team fold in late 2025, but it has not been as smooth sailing for the 23-year-old American at the club level.

After struggling for multiple seasons in Germany, first with Borussia Dortmund and then for a year at Borussia Monchengladbach, Reyna has found it difficult to break into either squad and earn a regular starting role.

So this season, Reyna dumped the Bundesliga and moved to France, where he joined BlueCo club Strasbourg hoping to turn his club career around.

Early signs are promising, as Reyna has slotted into a starting role with the club immediately under Portuguese manager Hugo Oliveria.

In the 14th minute of the Ligue 1 meeting between PSG and Strasbourg on Saturday at Stade de la Meinau, Gio Reyna gave the hosts an early lead as he snuck the ball in at the near post by Matvey Safanov.

The move was largely down to Reyna who created the moment for himself, first playing a give-and-go with right-winger Gessime Yassine before charging into the penalty area on the ball and picking out the inside of the near post.

The moment was a shock, as PSG were expected to walk the match against their opponents in the bottom half of the Ligue 1 table.

Reyna was everywhere for Strasbourg throughout the match, which represented his first 90-minute performance of the season. He saw 43 touches all over the pitch, with two early shots plus a chance created and a 27-for-32 passing effort.

Ultimately, Strasbourg would lose the match 3-1 to the Ligue 1 leaders, who scored three goals in the final 13 minutes of the game. Ilya Zabarnyi found the equalizer in the 77th minute, while substitutes Ousmane Dembele and Desire Doue came off the bench to secure the victory.

The goal was Gio Reyna's second of the season for Strasbourg, as he looks to carve out a regular role in France.

He has appeared in all seven of Strasbourg's league matches so far this season, with five of those starts, already more starts than he had all of last season in the Bundesliga with Borussia Monchengladbach.

His first goal for the club came in a 6-2 win over Troyes, scoring his team's third in the 57th minute.

Reyna has racked up 47 caps for the U.S. national team, scoring 10 goals in his international career.

articles.body:
An explanation for the early withdrawal of Barcelona star Gerard Martín during the club's latest outing has come to the fore online. This comes amid the understanding that the defender has picked up a minor fitness problem.

Martín was for his part in from the off once again this evening, as Barca made the trip to Seville for a La Liga meeting with high-flying Real Betis.

Upon the Blaugrana emerging from the tunnel for the 2nd-half, however, the Spaniard was nowhere to be seen, replaced by Eric García in the visitors' backline.

And as alluded to above, an explanation for precisely why has since surfaced in the Spanish media. As per a report from journalist Nil Sola:

'Gerard Martín substituted at halftime as a precaution. Ankle sprain, which hasn't worsened.'

Late in proceedings at La Cartuja, Hansi Flick's Blaugrana find themselves headed for another three-point haul, leading by four goals to two.

articles.title: Es para preocuparse... y mucho
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Betis-Barcelona
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Betis-Barcelona
articles.body: El Barcelona entra en su semana grande absolutamente lanzado, con once victorias en los once partidos que ha disputado. En Sevilla tuvo este sábado un partido titánico frente a un rival excelente que le complicó mucho las cosas. El equipo de Flick demostró que sigue en un momento de forma excelente y con una capacidad goleadora extraordinaria. Porque metió cinco, pero pudieron ser varios más. Y, dentro de ese nivel extraordinario, brilla con luz propia Lamine Yamal, que abrió el marcador a los nueve minutos y dio una excelente asistencia a Gabriel Jesús en el tercero. Ante el nivel del conjunto azulgrana, tanto Luis Enrique como Mourinho deberían estar realmente preocupados por lo que se les puede venir encima. Es cierto que tanto el PSG como el Real Madrid son dos rivales de enorme calidad, pero el momento de forma con el que llega el Barcelona no tiene parangón. Y este partido frente al Betis era una prueba muy importante para calibrar el estado de los culés. El único pero es la defensa, porque, como viene siendo habitual, encajan más goles de la cuenta. Lo del ataque es de otra galaxia. Tuvo lugar poco antes del descanso. Dos minutos después del 1-2 que consiguió Rodri, el Betis empató con un gol de Valentín Gómez. Sin embargo, De Burgos Bengoetxea lo anuló por una mano previa del Cucho Hernández. La mano parecía clara, pero los verdiblancos protestaron porque consideraban que el gol correspondía a una jugada distinta, ya que hubo un rechace del Barça. El colegiado no lo entendió así. En la segunda parte hubo más polémica con la expulsión de Facundo Bernal por darle un cabezazo a Lamine Yamal. El gol fue anulado, pero el gesto técnico de Lo Celso fue absolutamente espectacular. Según le llegó el balón, empalmó un excelente disparo a la escuadra de Joan García, que llegó a tocar el balón, pero no pudo evitar que entrara en su portería. Hansi Flick puso en liza un once muy competitivo. Pero, si el once era de gran calidad, lo del banquillo tiene su miga, porque con sus jugadores se podría formar un equipo que perfectamente podría ganar la Liga. Tomen nota: Livakovic, Cancelo, Eric, Bernal, Balde, Gavi, Fariñas, De Jong, Gordon, Olmo y Raphinha. Solo estos cuatro últimos jugadores le costaron al Barcelona más de 250 millones de euros. Todo un lujo. La historia volvió a repetirse. Uno de los problemas que tiene el Barcelona está en la parte de atrás: encaja más goles de los que debiera. Después del partido frente al Galatasaray, Rodri y Pedri se quejaron de este aspecto y, concretamente, de que el equipo turco marcó en la primera ocasión que tuvo. Frente al Betis ocurrió lo mismo. La primera ocasión que tuvo el equipo de Pellegrini acabó en gol. Un aspecto a mejorar. Además de pasar, organizar, dirigir y defender, le da por meter goles. Este es Rodri, un fichaje extraordinario por parte del Barcelona que está rindiendo a un excelente nivel en estos primeros partidos de la temporada. En La Cartuja marcó su primer gol como azulgrana. Aprovechó un buen saque de esquina de Fermín para cabecear el balón a la red.

articles.title: El Leipzig se hunde antes de visitar al Madrid: 'hat-trick' de Luis Díaz, recital de Kane y 'set' del Bayern
articles.standfirst: Los muniqueses se acuestan líderes provisionales a la espera de lo que haga el Friburgo
articles.summary: Los muniqueses se acuestan líderes provisionales a la espera de lo que haga el Friburgo
articles.body: Martín Demichelis, ex del Bayern, no tuvo su regreso soñado al Allianz Arena. 'Su' Leipzig encajó un 'set' (6-0) antes de visitar al Real Madrid en Champions. En el 12' ya ganaba 1-0. Luis Díaz recibió un pase de Kimmich a la espalda de Klostermann, desastroso, y definió mano a mano con Vandevoordt, que salvó a los 'toros' de una goleada, si cabe, más escandalosa. Era sólo el inicio. El recital de Luis Díaz continuó en el 26'. Kane filtró para el colombiano y éste cedió sobre la subida de Pavlovic, que fusiló con la zurda. El Bayern era un rodillo. Entre el poste y Vandevoordt evitaron que Olise hiciera el 3-0 en el 29'. No tardó en llegar. Perdió el Leipzig en salida, se giró de maravilla Kane y Olise marcó con un tiro cruzado para 'vengar' su expulsión en Champions ante el Vikingur (3-3). De poco o nada le valerion los cambios en el descanso -dio entrada a Gomis y Seiwald- a Demichelis. Volvió a perder en salida el Leipzig y Kane encontró a Luis Díaz, que amplió distancias en el 47' con un tiro al palo largo. Había repartido dos asistencias... pero le faltaba el gol a Kane. Llegó en el 52'. Luis Díaz cedió sobre la subida de Brown y éste puso el 'pase de la muerte' para el ex del Tottenham, que no perdonó. 102 goles acumula en 100 partidos en Bundesliga. Vandevoordt seguía acumulando manos salvadoras a disparos de Gnabry (64') y Bischof (69'). Nada pudo hacer para evitar el 'hat-trick' de Luis Díaz en el 69'. Recibió de Olise a la salida de un córner y volvió a marcar con un disparo al palo largo. El larguero y Vandevoordt evitaron el séptimo de Olise en el 75'. De hecho, el RB Leipzig terminó marcando el gol, golazo, del honor en el 91'. Gruda cedió atrás y Maksimokic la clavó en la escuadra. Poco importaba ya. El Bayern, a la espera de lo que haga el Friburgo, ya estabá en lo más alto de la tabla. Suma 14 puntos, los mismos que el Borussia Dortmund, pero tiene mejor diferencia de goles: +17 vs. +7.

articles.title: El Barça iguala el récord del Madrid
articles.standfirst: Con nueve triunfos consecutivos en el comienzo del campeonato
articles.summary: Con nueve triunfos consecutivos en el comienzo del campeonato
articles.body: El Barcelona sigue lanzado. Este sábado, en La Cartuja, ha conseguido su novena victoria consecutiva en Liga. Un triunfo que le permite igualar un nuevo récord, ya que alcanza la marca del Real Madrid en el número de partidos ganados de forma consecutiva al comienzo de la competición. El club blanco ostentaba la mejor marca tras encadenar nueve triunfos seguidos en la temporada 1968-1969. El equipo merengue estaba entonces entrenado por Miguel Muñoz y sumó esas nueve victorias consecutivas antes de empatar a cero en la décima jornada frente al Pontevedra. Con el triunfo en Sevilla, el Barcelona iguala este registro y ahora tendrá la oportunidad de superarlo en la próxima jornada. Además, se da la circunstancia de que su rival será el Real Madrid, en el Clásico que se disputará en el Spotify Camp Nou el domingo 25. El equipo de Hansi Flick se encuentra en un estado de forma extraordinario. Lo ha demostrado desde el comienzo de la competición en esta temporada. A los triunfos en Liga hay que sumar también las dos victorias que ha conseguido en la Champions frente al Feyenoord y al Galatasaray. Su extraordinario poder ofensivo ha sido clave para ganar todos los partidos que ha disputado. Ahora le esperan dos encuentros consecutivos muy complicados. El primero será el próximo martes frente al PSG, en la Champions. Los azulgranas visitarán el campo del actual campeón de Europa y tendrán muchas dificultades para mantener la racha frente al equipo de Luis Enrique. Posteriormente, durante el fin de semana, se verán las caras con el Real Madrid en un partido clave para evaluar sus opciones en la lucha por LaLiga.

articles.title: Brentford: Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet was 'cute and clever' for his part in Yehor Yarmoliuk's red card
articles.summary: Brentford took the lead through Keane Lewis-Potter at the Gtech Community Stadium, but Yehor Yarmoliuk's red card before half-time changed the game; "If you look at where Jacquet is walking, he's not looking at the ball, is he? He's walking in to Yarmo" - Bees boss Keith Andrews
articles.body:
Ukraine international Yarmoliuk was sent off in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time at the Gtech Community Stadium for catching Jacquet with what referee John Brooks called - after going to the VAR monitor - "a headbutting action".

The Reds defender went to ground in the box - but Andoni Iraola's men were not awarded a penalty as a corner on the left-hand side had not yet been delivered.

"We need to look at ourselves first, which we always do. We don't really tend to look at what part they played within the incident," said Andrews in his post-match press conference.

"I do think they were cute, clever - but Yarmo needs to do better, so I can understand why it was a red."

Asked what he meant, Andrews clarified: "If you look at where Jacquet is walking, he's not looking at the ball, is he? He's walking in to Yarmo."

A further follow-up asked if he felt Jacquet made the most of the contact.

"We focus on us and our actions within that and you can make up your own mind," he added.

"Yarmo is an amazing young man. I think we need to remember he is young, very young, and he is someone who we love working with and trying to develop. He will learn from it."

Goals from Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak turned the game in Liverpool's favour and Andrews conceded Yarmoliuk's sending off "changes the dynamics of the game".

To add insult to injury, his side ended the game with nine men after Vitaly Janelt was shown a second yellow card for bringing down Rio Ngumoha on the edge of the penalty area.

"I've seen both of Vitaly's yellows back and where I'm at overall is that I like our players playing with emotion. I think it's a big part of the way we play," he said.

"I like us to play on the edge and, when you do that and you feel like some decisions aren't fair, that can be very, very difficult for our players. I feel it and it can become very, very frustrating. Our players aren't robots.

"I'm more alluding to his first one. I think the second one is about his honesty to get back and chase back towards his own goal, which we have in abundance.

"We have a spirit within this team that I think is really, really special. Most midfielders wouldn't have been able to get back in to even challenge it.

"Could there have been a bit more common sense with the second yellow? I think so."

Iraola: VAR shouldn't have intervened on Liverpool penalty

Iraola, meanwhile, felt the officials were wrong to overturn the Liverpool penalty award before Lewis-Potter's Brentford opener.

Iraola agreed that Dango Ouattara touched the ball while challenging Alexis Mac Allister but insisted VAR should not have intervened, as was the case for Nottingham Forest's penalty against his side in their 2-2 draw at the City Ground in August.

Alisson was controversially penalised for fouling Neco Williams in that game but the key match incidents panel unanimously agreed that it did not reach the threshold for a VAR check and Iraola feels the same logic should have applied to Saturday's incident.

He said: "I think Dango touches the ball. I don't think it's a penalty. But also I don't think the VAR should intervene in that situation because there is clear contact after.

"I remember in the Nottingham Forest penalty against us this season, where they tell us it's not a penalty, VAR is not going to intervene because there is contact.

"So I think it's a very similar situation. I wouldn't call it a penalty, live.

"I think after watching the replay Dango arrives to touch the ball a little bit. But the way they explained to me the situation against Forest is exactly that one.

"I don't think the VAR should intervene."

articles.title: Premier League hits and misses: Liverpool ride their luck to win at Brentford
articles.summary: Sky Sports' football writers analyse Saturday's Premier League action as Chelsea win at Everton and Liverpool beat nine-man Brentford...
articles.body:
Liverpool spent close to £400m on Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola. Against Brentford, there was evidence that expensively-assembled attack might finally be clicking.

Isak was on the fringes of the game for long periods, limited to only 16 touches by the dogged hosts. But his brilliantly-taken goal, controlled and rifled home with dizzying speed in the second half, was a reminder of just how deadly he can be at his best.

It took him to five goals for the season. Only Erling Haaland has scored more in the Premier League. He is putting a difficult first season behind him and Andoni Iraola will be encouraged that it was Barcola who provided the assist.

The France international came into the game off the back of scoring a hat-trick against LASK in midweek and while he couldn't find the net against Brentford, missing a golden opportunity in the first half and hitting the bar in the second, Iraola liked what he saw.

"I love that he's having so many chances and being in those situations," said the Liverpool boss.

Then there was Wirtz, who provided the assist for Victor Munoz with a perfectly-weighted through-ball.

It was one of nine chances created - the joint-most by any Liverpool player in a single game since Opta started taking records in 2003/04. Nick Wright

Chelsea have the best front three in the Premier League but attack being the best form of defence for Xabi Alonso was never going to be sustainable. No team had conceded more goals than Chelsea's 13 after six Premier League matches.

But, in Saturday's 2-0 victory at Everton, they showed a different side to their game. Remarkably, this was not only Alonso's first clean sheet in the league since his appointment but also Chelsea's first clean sheet in the league for nine months.

Defensively, Chelsea have been a liability for some time. Alonso must fix that if his team are to take the leap and challenge again. The win at Everton was a step in the right direction. In the manager's words, Chelsea produced a "serious" and "mature" performance.

These are the characteristics that will differentiate Chelsea from most of the chasing pack in a Premier League season where seriousness is sorely lacking among some of the so-called 'Big Six'. Alonso, clearly, is a serious manager. Zinny Boswell

An ominous stat was provided by Opta during the build-up to Brentford's clash with Liverpool at the Gtech.

"Since their promotion to the top flight in 2021, the Bees have dropped more points from winning positions than any other side in the Premier League (102)."

A surprise, perhaps, given the Bees have taken to the top flight so well and finished in the top half in three of their first five seasons. And one that poses the question: what could have been?

For Brentford fans, that will not bear thinking about.

But that figure increased to 105 on Saturday, as they took the lead against the Reds before falling to a 2-1 defeat in a game they ended with nine men on the pitch.

Without the first of those reds - shown to Yehor Yarmoliuk before half-time, it might have been different. The reality? It's 11 points dropped for the season now, more than any other team in the division.

It has become a horrible habit - and one that needs kicking in to touch by Keith Andrews' men if those European ambitions are to materialise. Dan Long

Could this be the turning point in Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham reign?

It is certainly a start. With reports suggesting the Spaniard had two games to save his job, he needed a response and his players delivered one.

Fulham played with an intensity and attacking fluency that had been missing during their winless start to the Premier League season.

They registered 10 first-half shots, moved the ball quickly and repeatedly exposed a Hull side who struggled to impose themselves. Alex Iwobi's goal was deserved, but the hosts could easily have won by a greater margin.

There were encouraging signs of an identity taking shape, with the performance even prompting thoughts of 'Arbeloa-ball' at Craven Cottage.

Yet one result cannot erase the concerns of the opening weeks, and Fulham made the closing stages unnecessarily nervy before Ryan Sessegnon's stoppage-time red card.

The win lifts them out of the relegation zone and gives Arbeloa breathing space.

Whether it proves a turning point depends on what follows. For now, he has bought himself time and shown what his Fulham side can be. William Bitibiri
